scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 and PC4 in Campus 2 VLAN 6 report their gateway (10.6.0.254)
no longer responds. Other Campus 2 PCs (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5 on
VLAN 5) are fine. Identify the misconfiguration.

injection.action: change br_v6 SVI IP from .254 to .200
injection.command:
ip addr del 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6
  ip addr add 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v6 SVI IP address
Mechanism: PCs have their default route hard-coded to
  10.6.0.254 (the standard Cisco SVI VRRP-style address).
  sshswitch's br_v6 was reconfigured to 10.6.0.200, so
  ARP for 10.6.0.254 gets no reply — packets can't egress
  the subnet. The new address .200 IS reachable, but no host
  knows to use it.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v6 SVI IP set to 10.6.0.200 instead of 10.6.0.254
Fix: re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scenario.fix_spec:
re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: br_v6 SVI IP / VLAN 6 gateway IP

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the Layer‑3 SVI for Campus 2 VLAN 6 on the aggregation switch “sshswitch” (interface br_v6). Mechanism: PCs in VLAN 6 ARP and route to their configured default gateway 10.6.0.254. No device currently owns 10.6.0.254 on VLAN 6, so ARP requests go unanswered and ICMP to 10.6.0.254 fails with “Destination Host Unreachable,” even though L2 is intact. Localization: 
- On pc3/pc4, default route via 10.6.0.254 is present; pings to 10.6.0.254 fail. 
- pc3 can ping 10.6.0.200 and has an ARP entry for 10.6.0.200 at MAC 3a:e9:4f:48:6f:a0. 
- On sshswitch, br_v6 is configured as 10.6.0.200/24, not 10.6.0.254/24; arping for 10.6.0.254 on br_v6 gets no replies. 
- Switch4 shows VLAN 6 bridged correctly (eth4/eth5 access; trunk subinterface eth0.6), so L2 forwarding is fine. Root cause: misconfigured SVI address on sshswitch for VLAN 6 (set to 10.6.0.200 instead of the expected gateway 10.6.0.254). Corrective fix: reconfigure sshswitch br_v6 to use 10.6.0.254/24 (or temporarily add 10.6.0.254/24 as a secondary address) and remove 10.6.0.200/24 to restore the expected default gateway for VLAN 6. Example: ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6; ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6; then persist in the switch’s network config. VLAN 5 remains unaffected because its SVI is correctly set to 10.5.0.254 on sshswitch.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names the aggregation switch 'sshswitch' and localizes the misconfigured SVI (br_v6) to that device.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: br_v6 SVI IP / VLAN 6 gateway IP
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies the br_v6 SVI on sshswitch as having IP 10.6.0.200 instead of the expected VLAN 6 gateway 10.6.0.254.
Proposes removing the incorrect 10.6.0.200 address and assigning 10.6.0.254 to br_v6 (or adding it then removing the old IP), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains the key observations (pc reachability to .200, failed pings to .254, br_v6 set to .200 and arping for .254 failing, L2 appears up) that support the agent's diagnosis that the SVI was misconfigured. The writeup's inferences follow logically and the recommended fix addresses the root cause; only minor peripheral claims (VLAN5 SVI correctness) are not fully shown in the log.
